summary: The bill permanently adds all fentanyl-related substances—defined by any of five structural modifications to fentanyl—to Schedule I of the Controlled Substances Act, applies the same trafficking penalties as for fentanyl itself, and eases DEA registration rules for researchers studying Schedule I drugs.

scores.thoughts: This bill is primarily about drug policy, specifically by permanently scheduling fentanyl-related substances as Schedule I, which increases regulatory controls and penalties. It also streamlines research registration for controlled substances, but the main thrust is stricter control over fentanyl.

The bill directly impacts criminal justice by subjecting offenses involving fentanyl-related substances to the same quantity thresholds and mandatory minimum penalties as fentanyl analogues, including a 10-year mandatory minimum for certain quantities. This represents a move towards stricter justice for drug offenses.
